reason: The cited evidence supports the general use of Debye/Dulong–Petit extrapolations for cp and the role of configurational entropy in melting, but it does not provide specific prior experimental validation of the combined DSC-dilatometry-CALPHAD workflow for HEAs, nor does it demonstrate accuracy for fusion enthalpy, entropy, or volume change in these materials.
premises: DSC with Debye T^3 extrapolation and Dulong–Petit check yields accurate cp and thermal entropy for HEAs
DSC signal sharp increase at melting reliably gives Tm and latent heat
Combining DSC with dilatometry provides volume change at melting
CALPHAD modeling can validate and refine experimentally derived fusion parameters for HEAs
The approach works across a broad range of single-phase HEA compositions
